title: Immersive series-fidelity mode and screenreader briefs for time-series charts
creator: Anya Patel
description: Introduce an optional 'Fidelity mode' for time-series components that adjusts rendering fidelity, DOM verbosity, and screen-reader summaries based on user intent (immersive exploration vs quick-scan). The feature should reduce CPU and DOM load for low-fidelity / compact uses while exposing semantic, easily-navigable summaries for assistive tech. This ticket covers design decisions, interaction patterns, ARIA contract, and handoff artifacts for engineering to implement both canvas-based and DOM-backed fallbacks.
acceptance_criteria:
1) Fidelity mode toggle available in chart props and Console UI (compact | balanced | fidelity).
2) Compact mode reduces DOM nodes by >70% on large series (1000+ points) while preserving series color mapping and legend association.
3) Screenreader brief (aria-live polite) summarizing visible viewport min/max, trend (up/flat/down), and highlighted anomalies.
4) Keyboard-first navigation steps for legend items and annotations documented and prototyped.
5) Perf regression test added to dashboard: render time and main-thread JS reduced by target percentages for compact mode.
6) Design tokens defined for compact paddings, hit targets, and legend spacing.
7) Accessibility review completed and sign-off from a11y lead.
design_notes:
- Mode rationale: Many customers need two distinct workflows: exploratory sessions (high-fidelity, zoom, per-point hover) and production dashboards (compact, low-frequency updates). Consolidate into a single prop to avoid proliferating components.
- Compact rendering: prefer progressive decimation + sampled line rendering with canvas fallback. For DOM fallback, use aggregated polyline sr-only elements and summarized aria attributes instead of per-point DOM items.
- Legend behavior: in compact mode show condensed tokens (color square + short label) with numeric summary badge (visible count / last value). Provide an 'expand' affordance that lazily hydrates full legend DOM.
- Tooltip strategy: lightweight hover previews in compact (title + last value), full structured tooltip available on focus or expanded mode. Keep tooltips non-blocking and dismiss on pointerout.
- Screenreader briefs: produce a short 1-2 sentence summary via aria-live when viewport changes or when user tabs into the chart. Include series names (short), viewport range, trend direction, and top anomaly. Keep summaries concise to avoid TTS fatigue.
decisions:
- Use a single 'fidelity' chart prop (enum: compact|balanced|fidelity) rather than separate small/large components.
- Default to 'balanced' in Console; expose toggle in per-widget settings.
- Implement ARIA brief as aria-live='polite' region that receives synthesized summaries rather than exposing all points.
- Legend expand should be lazy-loaded to avoid initial DOM cost; expansion triggers analytics event.
- Performance targets: compact mode >50% reduction in main-thread time vs fidelity mode on 1k point series.

comments: 2026-03-02 - AP: Initial discovery: benchmarked current DOM count for 1k point series on Console widget. Baseline main-thread: ~210ms. Suggested target compact: <=100ms.
2026-03-04 - ER: Reviewed legend condensation mockups; request to show last-value micro-badge for each series in compact mode (ok'd).
2026-03-07 - ML (a11y): Requested examples of aria-live output and ensure summaries skip series that are visually hidden via toggles.

2026-03-10 - ENG (Marcus Huang): Feasibility check: will implement lazy hydrate for legend and aria brief; proposed API: fidelity: 'compact'|'balanced'|'fidelity', ariaBrief: boolean. Need design tokens from DS team for hit targets.
2026-03-12 - AP: Updated acceptance criteria to include perf dashboard and a11y sign-off. Added due date for stakeholder demo.
review_feedback: PM: favor a default of 'balanced' for new widgets; expose per-user preference later
Engineering: prefer explicit opt-in for aria-live summaries behind a feature flag to avoid TTS churn initially
Accessibility: keep summary sentences at ~10 words and avoid reading numeric microdata unless user requests details
